correctness.rationale: Feng's inclusive-scale formula at dimension five gives one S^4 and ten S^7 summands on the cover. The decisive integral basis certificate was checked directly: even first-three-bit parity and either fourth bit define a simplex in a coordinate four-face. An omitted vertex in that face has an even-parity complement at distance four. An outside vertex has a different fixed coordinate and differs from some simplex vertex in at least three free coordinates, so the simplex is globally maximal. Its indicator cocycle pairs by a unit with its own facet cycle and by zero with all other facet cycles. The ten unit pairings and the known rank give an integral basis. Complementation pairs the basis vectors up to orientation, which can be chosen compatibly, giving five regular modules. No simplex can contain an antipodal pair; there are no invariant simplices and the action is free. Its Lefschetz number is zero, so the rank-one degree-four action is minus one. In the mod-two Cartan–Leray sequence the degree-seven row is concentrated in column zero. Its classes are annihilated by t, whereas t acts injectively on the degree-four row at d_4, forcing that differential to vanish. If d_5 on the degree-four generator vanished, the same annihilator argument would rule out d_8 and leave unbounded cohomological degrees in a finite-dimensional quotient. Thus d_5 kills t^5 and all higher bottom-row powers, and t^4 survives as the actual covering-class power. Rational transfer gives the free rank; integral transfer kills all torsion by 2, since the cover has torsion-free homology. UCT and the mod-two dimensions then give one order-two summand in each of degrees one and three only. The integral Bockstein of t reduces to t^2 and its square reduces to t^4. All unlisted positive-degree products vanish by degree. The frozen verifier was not executed, and its full face census was not reproduced; the hand-checked maximal-simplex certificate and spectral sequence establish the stated groups and products without that optional census.

The fourth power of the actual covering class identifies a projective-type feature beyond the additive torsion list. The argument explains that feature by a forced differential rather than relying on an unexplained small-instance census.
